extracted.intended_audience: prospective improv students, performers, renters, and Chicago comedy audiences
extracted.subtask_description: Information and standards for classes, show formats, and venue rental at The Annoyance Theatre — emphasizing improv training that develops individual point of view and the structure/content of house shows. Useful for prospective students, performers planning shows, and event renters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annoyance improv philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annoyance philosophy focuses on the individual, giving students feedback and support to allow them to find and enhance their personal point of view and creative voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction is based on Artistic Director Mick Napier’s book Improvise: Scene From the Inside Out; teaching emphasizes individualized feedback and support rather than one-size-fits-all techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class instruction basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Improv classes are taught under the guidance of Artistic Director Mick Napier and grounded in the principles of his book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is presented as 'excellent quality' and uses Napier's methods (Improvise: Scene From the Inside Out) to develop students' creative voice; implication: instructors should follow these pedagogical methods and prioritize individual development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show content and tone (A Night of Unexpected Passion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows should present honest, joyful, passionate material where performers discuss unconventional passions and argue for their importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format examples: two queer comedians discuss unique passions with accompanying presentations and unapologetic enthusiasm; show features two different openers every week. Emphasize personality, persuasive enthusiasm, and variety in openers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show format example (Go West Young Man)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some shows combine music and comedy with a hosted format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a locally hosted evening of music and comedy led by a charismatic host; production should blend musical performance with comedic hosting and local personality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative output standard for the company
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annoyance uses improvisation to create new and original plays, musicals, sketch-comedy, and more in a vibrant, creative atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company output is expected to be original, derived from improv, and produced in a lively creative environment; productions aim for novelty and originality (examples given: Co-ed Prison Sluts, That Darned Antichrist, Splatter Theater).

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue rental specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Spaces available for rent include 6 studio classrooms, a Small (40 seat) theater, and a Mainstage (100 seat) theater; they may be rented for rehearsals, meetings, auditions, commercial use (classes/workshops), corporate/special events and parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studios suited for rehearsals/meetings/auditions or commercial classes; theaters available for events with stated seating capacities; rental follows commercial rates and can be used for a variety of purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programming frequency and audience engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annoyance runs shows 7 days a week and encourages visitors to catch a show, hang out at the bar, take a class and meet performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectation for continuous programming and an integrated audience/bar/class experience; venue positioning emphasizes accessibility and community-building through frequent shows and ancillary activities.
